heroHeadline: Iran Federation President Denied Entry to Canada — Sports Minister: 'Under No Circumstances' Can Iran Participate; FIFA Congress Opens in Vancouver Without Iran; 42 Days to Kickoff
heroSubtitle: The Iranian participation crisis reached a breaking point on April 30: Football Federation President Mehdi Taj and two senior officials arrived at Toronto Pearson International Airport with valid visas but were refused entry to Canada — Canadian authorities cited Taj's alleged ties to the IRGC, which Canada designated a terrorist organization in 2024. The three officials returned to Turkey and missed the 76th FIFA Congress entirely. Within hours, Iran Sports Minister Ahmad Donyamali issued his most definitive statement: Iran 'under no circumstances' can participate in the 2026 World Cup. Iran's pre-tournament warm-up friendlies were simultaneously cancelled. If Iran formally withdraws, it would be the first country to do so after qualifying since 1950. Iran International identified Taj's IRGC links as the specific legal basis for the Canadian refusal; FIFA said Infantino would meet the delegation in Zurich. The FIFA Congress, opened April 30 at the Vancouver Convention Centre by 1,600+ delegates, formally convened amid the Iran crisis — with CAF's 54 member associations unanimously endorsing Infantino's re-election for a 2027–2031 term. An NPR report published the same day documented international fans choosing to skip the tournament due to unaffordable ticket prices and US immigration enforcement anxiety. Iran's Group G matches (Los Angeles: June 15 vs New Zealand, June 21 vs Belgium; Seattle: June 26 vs Egypt) remain on the schedule pending any official withdrawal. 42 days to kickoff at Estadio Azteca.
